Plasma Glucose Requirement for CRU Admission/Dosing
data.description: Admission can be rescheduled if plasma glucose is outside the required range on Day 1
data.text: Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Hypoglycemia Induction Target (Insulin Infusion Stop)
data.description: Threshold for stopping the IV insulin infusion prior to study treatment administration
data.text: The insulin infusion will be stopped once the PG level reaches <60 mg/dL and approximately 5 minutes later patients will be administered either 3 mg LY900018 or 1 mg IMG (GlucaGen).

data.name: Edinburgh Scale 'During Hypoglycemia Induction' Trigger
data.description: Timing condition for the during-induction administration of the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale
data.text: During hypoglycemia induction will be when PG ≤75 mg/dL.

data.name: Interim Safety Review After First 6 Patients
data.description: Dosing of remaining patients is gated on review of safety data from the first 6 patients who received LY900018 in Period 2
data.text: Safety data will be reviewed after the first 6 patients (regardless of type of diabetes) are administered LY900018 in Period 2, and the remaining patients will be dosed after confirmation of the safety. The investigator and Lilly CRP or scientist will review available safety data, including AEs, SAEs, vital signs, ECGs, and safety laboratory tests, from these patients after they complete Period 2 Day 1. If no clinically significant safety findings for treatment or study procedure are noted, the remaining patients will be dosed.

data.name: Treatment-Emergent ADA Condition for Additional Follow-up
data.description: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED undergo additional immunogenicity follow-up
data.text: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED will undergo additional follow-up. Samples for immunogenicity should be collected every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until the titer returns to baseline (ie, returns to within a single 2-fold dilution of the baseline titer) or until 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Insufficient Response to Glucagon Administration
data.description: Protocol-specified procedures are followed when response to glucagon administration is insufficient
data.text: Procedures for Insufficient Response to Glucagon Administration (Section 9.2.4).

data.name: Non-inferiority Decision Criterion
data.description: Statistical condition for declaring non-inferiority of LY900018
data.text: Non-inferiority of LY900018 will be declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% CI constructed on the difference in percentage (IMG - LY900018) is less than the NIM of 10%.

data.name: Completer/Sample Size Condition
data.description: Enrollment and replacement conditions to reach required number of completers
data.text: Seventy five patients may be enrolled in order to have at least 66 patients (at least 30 patients with T1DM and T2DM, respectively) complete both periods with evaluable primary outcome. Replacement should not occur beyond 75 patients enrolled, if it is expected to have at least 66 patients complete the study.

data.name: Discharge Condition After Glucagon Administration
data.description: Conditions required before discharge from the CRU
data.text: Patient may be discharged 6 hours after glucagon administration. A patient may remain inpatient at the CRU at the discretion of the investigator. All patients will receive a carbohydrate-rich meal prior to discharge and the investigator will ensure the patient's PG is stable.

data.name: Insulin Regimen Acceptability for Hypoglycemia Induction
data.description: Review of concomitant insulin regimens prior to the induction procedure
data.text: Review patients' insulin regimens to confirm acceptability to undergo the procedure to induce hypoglycemia.

data.name: Period 2 Timing Consistency Condition
data.description: Period 2 procedures must occur at approximately the same clock time as Period 1
data.text: Procedures in Period 2 will occur at approximately the same time as those in Period 1.

data.name: Screening to Period 1 Transition
data.text: Patients will undergo a screening examination within 28 days prior to enrollment and must meet enrollment criteria; admission to the CRU occurs on Period 1 Day -1 and admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Randomization to Treatment Sequence
data.text: Prior to the study drug administration on Period 1 Day 1, patients will be randomly assigned to a treatment sequence (either LY900018 in Period 1 and IMG in Period 2, or vice versa).

data.name: Period 1 to Washout to Period 2 Crossover Transition
data.text: Patients will be administered a single dose in Periods 1 and 2, which will be separated by a washout period of 3 to 14 days.

data.name: Period 2 to Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients will return for a follow-up visit 26 to 30 days after the last study treatment (within 28±2 days after last study treatment).

data.name: Follow-up to Additional TE ADA Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED will undergo additional follow-up with immunogenicity samples collected every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until the titer returns to baseline or until 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Gated Dosing After Interim Safety Review
data.text: The remaining patients will be dosed after confirmation of safety based on review of data from the first 6 patients who completed Period 2 Day 1; if no clinically significant safety findings for treatment or study procedure are noted, the remaining patients will be dosed.

data.name: Discontinuation of Inadvertently Enrolled Patients
data.text: If the sponsor or investigator identifies a patient who did not meet enrollment criteria and was inadvertently enrolled, a discussion must occur between the Lilly CP/CRP and the investigator to determine if the patient may continue in the study. If both agree it is medically appropriate to continue, the investigator must obtain documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP to allow the patient to continue with or without continued treatment with investigational product.

data.name: Discontinuation for Enrollment in Another Study
data.text: Patients will be discontinued for enrollment in any other clinical study involving an investigational product or enrollment in any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study.

data.name: Discontinuation for Medical, Safety, or Regulatory Reasons
data.text: Participation in the study needs to be stopped for medical, safety, regulatory, or other reasons consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and good clinical practice.

data.name: Discontinuation by Investigator Decision
data.text: The investigator decides that the patient should be discontinued from the study for any reason. If this decision is made because of an AE, SAE, or a severe hypoglycemia event, appropriate measures are to be taken. Lilly or its designee is to be alerted.

data.name: Discontinuation by Patient Decision
data.text: The patient, or legal representative, requests to be withdrawn from the study.

data.name: Rescue for Insufficient Response to Glucagon
data.text: Procedures for insufficient response to glucagon administration will be followed (Section 9.2.4); a carbohydrate-rich meal is provided after completion of all PK sampling and a prandial insulin dose will be administered if needed to ensure PG stability.

data.name: Rescheduling of Admission/Dosing
data.text: Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Early Discontinuation (ED)
data.description: Patients discontinuing from the study prematurely for any reason must complete AE and follow-up procedures as shown in the Schedule of Activities; the Follow-up/ED visit serves as the early discontinuation visit.

data.name: Study Completion
data.description: Completion of both treatment periods with an evaluable primary outcome and the follow-up visit occurring 26 to 30 days (within 28±2 days) after the last study treatment, including any additional TE ADA follow-up until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Lost to Follow-up
data.description: A patient will be considered lost to follow-up if he or she repeatedly fails to return for scheduled visits and is unable to be contacted by the study site, after diligent attempts at contact.

data.name: Discontinuation of the Study (Safety Stopping Rule)
data.description: Following review of the safety data from the first 6 patients to complete Period 2 Day 1, the study will be stopped if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the investigator and sponsor.

data.name: Exit for Inadvertent Enrollment (Did Not Meet Criteria)
data.description: Patients inadvertently enrolled who did not meet enrollment criteria may be discontinued unless documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP is obtained to continue.

data.name: CRU Admission/Dosing Eligibility Decision
data.description: On Day 1 of each period, dosing proceeds only if PG level is 90 to 250 mg/dL; otherwise admission is rescheduled.

data.name: Insulin Infusion Stop / Dosing Decision
data.description: Insulin infusion is stopped once bedside PG is <60 mg/dL and study drug is administered approximately 5 minutes later (Time = 0 min).

data.name: Interim Safety Review Decision (First 6 Patients)
data.description: After the first 6 patients complete Period 2 Day 1, the investigator and Lilly CRP/scientist review safety data to decide whether remaining patients may be dosed or the study stopped.

data.name: TE ADA Additional Follow-up Decision
data.description: At Follow-up/ED, patients with treatment-emergent ADA enter additional immunogenicity follow-up every 84±7 days until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Insufficient Glucagon Response Decision
data.description: Post glucagon administration, the investigator determines whether response is insufficient and applies Section 9.2.4 procedures.

data.name: Discharge Decision
data.description: Patient may be discharged 6 hours after glucagon administration following a carbohydrate-rich meal and stable PG, or remain inpatient at investigator discretion.

data.name: Primary Non-inferiority Analysis Decision
data.description: Primary analysis compares treatment success percentages; non-inferiority declared if upper limit of 2-sided 95% CI for (IMG - LY900018) is <10%, based on at least 66 completers.
